rationale: C18 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. The child closely reproduces its distinctive two-part operative structure and much of its wording: first asking the people to honor the flag by displaying it at homes or other suitable places and reflecting on citizenship, then directing officials to display the flag on Government buildings. C17 and C19 are also strong same-series precedents, but their operative language is less nearly identical to the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby ask that on Flag Day, June 14, 1954, the people of the Nation honor our colors by displaying them at their homes or other suitable places
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby ask that on Flag Day, June 14, 1949, the people of the Nation honor our colors by displaying them at their homes or other suitable places
shared_material.explanation: This is nearly verbatim language, with principally the annual date changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: by giving prayerful consideration to their duties as well as their privileges as citizens under this glorious banner
shared_material.parent_excerpt: by giving thanks for their privileges as citizens under this flag as well as by engaging in earnest contemplation of the obligations inherent in citizenship
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same distinctive reflective appeal contrasting citizens' privileges with their duties or obligations under the flag.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also direct the appropriate officials of the Government to arrange for the display of the flag on all Government buildings on that day.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I also direct the appropriate officials of the Government to display the flag of the United States on all Government buildings on Flag Day.
shared_material.explanation: The second operative sentence preserves substantially the same governmental direction, wording, and sequence.
